results.name: set_level_sd_nonexample_rate
results.description: Standard deviation across 2-4 example sets of each set's yes rate for non-example targets; observed above null means the model is too homogeneous across sets (people generalize much more broadly from some sets and much more narrowly from others than the model's concept posterior implies).
results.code:
# name: set_level_sd_nonexample_rate
# description: Standard deviation across 2-4 example sets of each set's yes rate for non-example targets; observed above null means the model is too homogeneous across sets (people generalize much more broadly from some sets and much more narrowly from others than the model's concept posterior implies).
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4)).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(E)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    Ez = np.where(valid, E, 0.0)
    lo = np.where(valid, E, np.inf).min(axis=1)
    hi = np.where(valid, E, -np.inf).max(axis=1)
    is_ex = (valid & (E == t[:, None])).any(axis=1)
    odd = (np.where(valid, Ez % 2, 1) == 1).all(axis=1)
    even = (np.where(valid, Ez % 2, 0) == 0).all(axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    m = (n >= 2) & ~is_ex
    s = pd.Series(y[m]).groupby(df["number_set"].to_numpy()[m]).mean()
    return float(s.std()) if len(s) > 1 else 0.0

results.name: two_example_in_minus_out_range
results.description: On 2-example sets, yes rate for non-example targets inside [min, max] minus yes rate for targets outside it; observed above null means the model's generalization from two examples is not range-confined enough (too little inside, too much outside).
results.code:
# name: two_example_in_minus_out_range
# description: On 2-example sets, yes rate for non-example targets inside [min, max] minus yes rate for targets outside it; observed above null means the model's generalization from two examples is not range-confined enough (too little inside, too much outside).
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4)).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(E)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    Ez = np.where(valid, E, 0.0)
    lo = np.where(valid, E, np.inf).min(axis=1)
    hi = np.where(valid, E, -np.inf).max(axis=1)
    is_ex = (valid & (E == t[:, None])).any(axis=1)
    odd = (np.where(valid, Ez % 2, 1) == 1).all(axis=1)
    even = (np.where(valid, Ez % 2, 0) == 0).all(axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    base = (n == 2) & ~is_ex
    inr = (t >= lo) & (t <= hi)
    return rate(base & inr) - rate(base & ~inr)

results.name: two_example_multiples_opposite_parity
results.description: On 2-example same-parity sets whose examples are all multiples of some k in {3,4,6,7,8,9,11,12} (largest such k) and do not share a last digit, yes rate for non-example targets that are multiples of k but of the opposite parity (e.g. 28 after 7,63); observed above null means the model lets parity block arithmetic-rule extension too strongly (people extend the multiples rule across parity).
results.code:
# name: two_example_multiples_opposite_parity
# description: On 2-example same-parity sets whose examples are all multiples of some k in {3,4,6,7,8,9,11,12} (largest such k) and do not share a last digit, yes rate for non-example targets that are multiples of k but of the opposite parity (e.g. 28 after 7,63); observed above null means the model lets parity block arithmetic-rule extension too strongly (people extend the multiples rule across parity).
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4)).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(E)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    Ez = np.where(valid, E, 0.0)
    lo = np.where(valid, E, np.inf).min(axis=1)
    hi = np.where(valid, E, -np.inf).max(axis=1)
    is_ex = (valid & (E == t[:, None])).any(axis=1)
    odd = (np.where(valid, Ez % 2, 1) == 1).all(axis=1)
    even = (np.where(valid, Ez % 2, 0) == 0).all(axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    k = np.zeros(len(t))
    for kk in [3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12]:
        allm = (np.where(valid, Ez % kk, 0) == 0).all(axis=1)
        k = np.where(allm, kk, k)
    ld = np.where(valid, Ez % 10, np.nan)
    shared = (np.where(valid, ld == ld[:, [0]], True)).all(axis=1)
    kk_safe = np.where(k > 0, k, 1).astype(int)
    tm = (k > 0) & (t % kk_safe == 0)
    opp = np.where(odd, t % 2 == 0, np.where(even, t % 2 == 1, False))
    m = (n == 2) & (odd | even) & ~shared & ~is_ex & tm & opp
    return rate(m)

results.name: four_example_same_parity_opposite_targets
results.description: On 4-example sets whose examples are all odd or all even, yes rate for non-example targets of the opposite parity; observed below null means the model over-generalizes across parity after four same-parity examples (people treat parity as more binding than the model).

    hi = np.where(valid, E, -np.inf).max(axis=1)

results.name: single_example_prime_minus_mult5
results.description: On one-example sets, yes rate for non-example targets when the lone example is prime minus when it is a multiple of 5; observed below null means the model generalizes too much from a lone prime (over-weights the prime rule) and/or too little from a lone round number (under-weights multiples of 5/10).
results.code:
# name: single_example_prime_minus_mult5
# description: On one-example sets, yes rate for non-example targets when the lone example is prime minus when it is a multiple of 5; observed below null means the model generalizes too much from a lone prime (over-weights the prime rule) and/or too little from a lone round number (under-weights multiples of 5/10).
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4)).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(E)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    Ez = np.where(valid, E, 0.0)
    lo = np.where(valid, E, np.inf).min(axis=1)
    hi = np.where(valid, E, -np.inf).max(axis=1)
    is_ex = (valid & (E == t[:, None])).any(axis=1)
    odd = (np.where(valid, Ez % 2, 1) == 1).all(axis=1)
    even = (np.where(valid, Ez % 2, 0) == 0).all(axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    x = Ez[:, 0].astype(int)
    isp = np.ones(len(x), dtype=bool) & (x > 1)
    for a in range(2, 11):
        isp &= ~((x % a == 0) & (x != a))
    base = (n == 1) & ~is_ex
    return rate(base & isp) - rate(base & (x % 5 == 0))

results.name: shared_digit_3plus_nonmatching_same_parity
results.description: On 3-4 example sets whose examples all share a last digit, yes rate for non-example targets with a different last digit but the same parity as the examples; observed below null means the model (even with explaining away) still leaks too much generalization to same-parity / contains-digit numbers when an ends-in-digit rule fits.
results.code:
# name: shared_digit_3plus_nonmatching_same_parity
# description: On 3-4 example sets whose examples all share a last digit, yes rate for non-example targets with a different last digit but the same parity as the examples; observed below null means the model (even with explaining away) still leaks too much generalization to same-parity / contains-digit numbers when an ends-in-digit rule fits.
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4)).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(E)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    Ez = np.where(valid, E, 0.0)
    lo = np.where(valid, E, np.inf).min(axis=1)
    hi = np.where(valid, E, -np.inf).max(axis=1)
    is_ex = (valid & (E == t[:, None])).any(axis=1)
    odd = (np.where(valid, Ez % 2, 1) == 1).all(axis=1)
    even = (np.where(valid, Ez % 2, 0) == 0).all(axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    ld = np.where(valid, Ez % 10, np.nan)
    first = ld[:, 0]
    shared = (np.where(valid, ld == first[:, None], True)).all(axis=1)
    same_par = np.where(odd, t % 2 == 1, np.where(even, t % 2 == 0, False))
    m = (n >= 3) & shared & ~is_ex & ((t % 10) != first) & same_par
    return rate(m)
